headline: Funding flows. Contracts expand. Plans derail.
deck: This week saw significant funding rounds and contract modifications as the space industry grapples with shifting priorities.

stories.head: Iceye raises €1 billion for satellite expansion
stories.body: Iceye has raised over €1 billion to expand its radar imaging satellite systems, underscoring the growing demand for satellite data. This move positions Iceye as a key player in the SAR market, where competition is heating up. The funding round is a clear indicator that investors are still keen on space ventures, despite broader economic uncertainties.
stories.soWhat: When satellite data is hot, it’s not just the tech that shines; it’s the investors looking for the next big return.

stories.head: BlackSky accelerates AROS satellite work for NRO
stories.body: BlackSky has received a contract modification from the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) to expedite its AROS satellite development. This modification signals an increasing urgency in the intelligence community for timely satellite data, especially amidst rising geopolitical tensions. With this push, BlackSky is likely to enhance its competitive edge in the spy satellite race.
stories.soWhat: In the intelligence game, speed can be as critical as accuracy; BlackSky is betting that quicker satellites will win contracts.

stories.head: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant clears design review
stories.body: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser DoD variant has successfully passed its critical design review, paving the way for further development. This marks a significant milestone as the company aims to fulfill Department of Defense requirements for cargo transport. However, the real challenge lies ahead in transitioning from design to actual deployment, a hurdle many have stumbled over.
stories.soWhat: Design reviews are the easy part; execution is where dreams often get grounded.

watchlist.title: Watch for more funding rounds
watchlist.body: With Iceye's massive raise, other companies may follow suit to capitalize on investor interest in space.

watchlist.title: NRO’s procurement strategy shifts
watchlist.body: BlackSky's contract modification may indicate a broader shift in NRO priorities towards rapid satellite deployment.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space’s next steps
watchlist.body: The success of Dream Chaser’s design review will be closely monitored as it moves toward production.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly’s growth trajectory
watchlist.body: Following its $190M Series C, True Anomaly's strategic moves will be key in the co-orbital security sector.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
